task_1.title: Keep the `hash` argument supported without deprecation warnings
task_1.description: The upgrade changes the deprecation policy for the `hash` argument on attrs class-definition APIs. Existing uses of `hash` should continue to work without deprecation warnings, while `unsafe_hash` remains the preferred explicit override when both options are present.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 24.2.0 preserves compatibility for applications that still pass the `hash` argument to attrs class-definition APIs, eliminating deprecation-warning noise while keeping hashing behavior stable and allowing `unsafe_hash` to remain the effective override.

expectation.grounded: Passing `hash` to the `define` / `attr.s` class decorators must remain supported as a soft-deprecated API and must no longer emit a `DeprecationWarning`. Passing `hash` to `make_class` must also remain accepted and continue to configure hashing behavior. If both `hash` and `unsafe_hash` are supplied, `unsafe_hash` must take precedence.
expectation.conceptual: Existing code that still uses the older `hash` option should continue to work quietly after the upgrade. The option remains discouraged for new code, but it is not being removed, and newer hash settings should still override it when both are provided.

constraints.grounded: Do not turn use of the `hash` keyword into an error or removal-triggering deprecation. Do not change the resulting hash configuration semantics for existing callers beyond suppressing deprecation warnings. Preserve precedence of `unsafe_hash` over `hash`.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should reduce ecosystem warning noise without forcing migrations or changing the effective hashing behavior that callers already rely on.

behavior: Using the `hash` argument with the `define` or `attr.s` decorators no longer emits a deprecation warning.
Using the `hash` argument with `make_class` remains accepted and continues to control the resulting class hash behavior.
The `hash` argument is treated as soft-deprecated rather than scheduled for removal.
When both `hash` and `unsafe_hash` are provided, the effective hash configuration follows `unsafe_hash`.
acceptance_criteria: When a class is declared with `define(hash=True)` or `attr.s(hash=True)`, class creation should succeed without a deprecation warning and the resulting class should be configured for hashing accordingly.
When a class is declared with `define(hash=False)` or `attr.s(hash=False)`, class creation should succeed without a deprecation warning and hashing should remain disabled accordingly.
When `make_class` is called with a `hash` argument, dynamic class creation should succeed without a deprecation warning and the resulting class should reflect the requested hash policy.
When both `hash` and `unsafe_hash` are provided to attrs class-definition APIs, the observable hashing behavior should follow `unsafe_hash`.

task_3.title: Restore attrs annotation compatibility for Python 3.14 semantics
task_3.description: Attrs 24.2.0 restores core support for Python runtimes adopting PEP 649 and PEP 749 annotation semantics, especially Python 3.14 development builds, by switching annotation lookup to the interpreter-provided annotations API where needed instead of assuming annotations are always available as a plain class dictionary entry.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that annotation-based attrs class definitions continue to work on Python runtimes implementing PEP 649 / 749 semantics, including Python 3.14-style deferred annotations, so annotated fields are still discovered during class creation.

expectation.grounded: When attrs inspects class annotations during class creation, it should use a compatibility-layer annotation lookup that calls `annotationlib.get_annotations` on Python 3.14 and newer, while preserving the existing `__annotations__` dictionary lookup on earlier Python versions. Annotation-driven attrs usage, including `attr.s(..., auto_attribs=True)` and equivalent annotation-based class building flows, should continue to recognize annotated attributes on PEP 649 / 749 interpreters.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to keep defining attrs classes with type-annotated fields on newer Python runtimes with deferred annotation semantics, and attrs should interpret those annotations correctly without requiring user code changes just because the interpreter changed how annotations are stored.

constraints.grounded: The compatibility change must be version-sensitive: Python versions before 3.14 must retain the previous annotation lookup behavior, and classes with no annotations must still be handled as having an empty annotation mapping. The upgrade should change annotation retrieval compatibility only, not the visible contract of attrs class construction beyond restoring support on PEP 649 / 749 runtimes.
constraints.conceptual: Add support for the new interpreter annotation model without regressing behavior on already supported Python versions or changing how annotation-based attrs declarations behave for users.

behavior: On Python 3.14 and newer, attrs retrieves class annotations through the runtime annotation API instead of directly depending on `__annotations__` being present in the class dictionary.
On Python versions earlier than 3.14, attrs continues to obtain class annotations from the class `__annotations__` mapping as before.
Annotation-dependent attrs class construction regains basic functionality on interpreters implementing PEP 649 / 749 semantics.
If a class has no annotations, attrs treats the annotation set as empty rather than failing during annotation lookup.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Python runtime with PEP 649 / 749-style annotation behavior, when a user defines an attrs class using annotated fields, attrs should discover those annotations during class creation instead of behaving as though they are missing.
Given a Python version earlier than 3.14, when attrs inspects class annotations, it should preserve the prior behavior based on the class `__annotations__` mapping.
When an attrs class has no annotations, annotation lookup should produce an empty result and class creation should continue without an annotation-lookup failure.
After upgrading to 24.2.0, users relying on annotation-based attrs declarations should regain basic compatibility on Python 3.14 development-era runtimes without changing their public attrs usage.

task_2.title: Restore attrs converter pipelines during attribute assignment
task_2.description: attrs 24.2.0 fixes a regression where converter pipelines created with attrs.converters.pipe() or list-style converter declarations stopped working correctly when attribute assignment used attrs.setters.convert, including the default on_setattr behavior of attrs.define. The update also ensures Converter wrappers adapt calls with instance and field context correctly and preserves observable return-type metadata for piped converters.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that converter pipelines declared with attrs.converters.pipe() or list-style converter syntax continue to work correctly during both initialization and later attribute assignment when on_setattr includes attrs.setters.convert, including the default behavior of attrs.define.

expectation.grounded: When a field or attribute uses a converter pipeline, each stage must be invoked correctly whether it is a plain callable or an attrs.Converter. attrs.Converter instances must receive value-only, value plus instance, value plus field, or value plus instance and field according to their takes_self and takes_field configuration. During on_setattr conversion, attrs.setters.convert must call attrs.Converter-based converters with the current instance and attribute metadata so reassignment yields the same converted result as initialization. If the last converter in a pipeline is an annotated attrs.Converter, the pipeline should retain the wrapped return-type annotation for public introspection.
expectation.conceptual: Converter chains should behave consistently when objects are created and when attributes are reassigned later. Converters that declare instance-aware or field-aware behavior should keep receiving that context, reassignment should apply the same conversion semantics as construction, and public typing or introspection metadata exposed by the converter chain should stay accurate.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing behavior for plain one-argument converters and for attributes that do not use conversion on assignment. Keep list-based converter declarations equivalent to an explicit attrs.converters.pipe() chain, and do not alter the declared takes_self or takes_field semantics of attrs.Converter.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be backward-compatible for existing simple converters and non-converting setters, while restoring correct behavior only for converter pipelines and context-aware converters.

behavior: A converter list supplied through converter= must continue to act as a pipeline during assignment as well as during initialization.
attrs.converters.pipe() must execute attrs.Converter stages using the same context-aware calling convention they require outside the pipeline.
When attrs.setters.convert runs for an attribute whose converter is an attrs.Converter, it must pass the active instance and attribute descriptor when the converter declares that it uses them.
Pipelines whose final stage is an annotated attrs.Converter must continue to expose the wrapped return type through public annotation introspection.
acceptance_criteria: When an attrs.define class declares a field with converter=[int], assigning a new string value after initialization should store the converted integer value.

When a field uses a converter pipeline built with attrs.converters.pipe() or list syntax and assignment conversion is enabled, assigning a new value should run the full pipeline in order and persist the final converted result.

When a pipeline contains an attrs.Converter configured with takes_self and/or takes_field, conversion during assignment should pass the current instance and/or attribute metadata exactly for the enabled flags.
When the last stage of a converter pipeline is an annotated attrs.Converter, introspection of the pipeline should report the wrapped return type rather than dropping that annotation.
